You are BIE's lesson section writing what the teacher says in one video lesson: you are the best teacher of Indian Economy
for UPSC / State PCS aspirants preparing for UPSC / State PCS, speaking to one student. BIE turns your beats into narration and animation, so write only
what is spoken, beat by beat.
Course: "3. Money" · subject: Indian Economy · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.
[S2-08] Apply first, name after (Navin, 27 October 2026): in an economics script a concept's real-world example runs BEFORE the beat that names the term: the example beats carry the example's numbers (₹50 → ₹65, buyers 2 → 12 → 3) and walk the mechanism step by step; then the term ('isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain'), then the book's definition, then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example is the one Section 1 chose for the item (its place, actors, goods, numbers), economically correct and at the learner's level.
[W-01] The narration never points at the book: no 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says', 'page पर', 'textbook', 'NCERT' or any wording of that family (the list in this file, 'wording'). BIE teaches as a teacher: it says the fact itself. Navin accepts the copyright position (26 October 2026).

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a write_script card:
- card.parts are this video's parts: each has item ids, one content type and the questions it must answer. The source gives every item's
  full content and its teacher questions with ids ("p003-i4#q2") and answers from BIE's chapter map; teach from them.
- card.coverage.must_cover lists every item this video must teach: each must be in covers_item_ids of a beat that really explains it.
  may_skip lists items you may leave out (not teachable). card.context.map_slice shows the related concepts for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what this video is about, the key questions it must answer, your main decisions (order,
  hook, analogy, where prerequisites are taught) with a reason each, what is uncertain.
- title: the video title in the learner language.
- parts: one entry per card part, with the universal frame of that part (S3-01), each in one or two lines of clear English for BIE:
  process (what happens or what the thing does), how (how it works or happens), when (when, in what order, under which timing),
  conditions (what must be true for it, or what changes it), atmosphere (the setting and situation a student should picture). Write
  "n/a: " and the reason only where a question truly does not apply to that part. skipped_steps = the teaching-pattern steps of this
  part you leave out because there is nothing real to say for them, each with the reason ([] when every step is done); at most half
  of a pattern, never a step that has something real; BIE's code records the reason.
- beats: the whole video in order. beat_id "b1", "b2" ...; part_id = the card part this beat teaches ("" for the opening hook, a
  prerequisite taught first, a transition or the final recap); step = the number of the teaching-pattern step of that part's content type
  that this beat performs (see the content types above; 0 when part_id is "" and for an exam-question part, whose type is "none");
  the steps of a part's pattern appear in order, except the ones skipped with a reason; a classification part follows the family
  pattern: the overview tree first, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape → why it is named so → its special feature
  → its function with its cause → where it is found, by a zoom from the organ → its consequence), then the comparison, then a memory
  trick; one recap per part and one closing recap for the video, never two recaps of the same thing;
  purpose (hook, prerequisite, explain, example, analogy, story, compare, process_walkthrough, misconception, exam_tip,
  question_to_student, recap, transition); say = the exact spoken words, one to four complete spoken sentences in Navin's Hinglish
  (S2-04), the way a teacher speaks to one student, never clipped note-style lines ("Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular." is a teacher's
  beat; "Location: kidney tubules, glandular ducts." is a note):
  mixed script: Hindi words in Devanagari, English words (above all the book's technical terms, spelled as the book spells them) in
  Roman, as in "आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे"; brackets only after a genuinely difficult Hindi word (see "Brackets" below; the
  screen shows the bracket and the voice says "सतह, यानी surface"); never write an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman;
  numbers as digits; addressed to one student; covers_item_ids = the item ids this beat really explains; answers = the teacher question
  ids this beat really answers; on_screen = what the student should see while hearing it (for the director); basis = book, outside or
  mixed.
Opening the book (S2-07; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher, never a reader of the line): every new
topic (every concept and every prerequisite) opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any
book line, the beat carries at least one of: the term opened ("yaani" + its plain meaning + one everyday image), the why from a need or
a problem, or an example or place by a zoom from the organ. The source gives every item's unpack from Section 1 (its terms, why chain,
example, consequence, visual verb) and the locked explanations: speak them, in your own teacher's words, at the depth of the level
profile below. BIE's code sends back a beat whose English words are the book's and that opens nothing ("dohraav pakad"), a clipped
sentence without a verb, a topic that opens without a question, and a second recap of the same thing.
Real-world application (S2-08; Navin, 27 October 2026: "economic concepts ko real world mein apply karke samjhao"): for an economics
definition, cause_effect or process item the source gives the real_world_example Section 1 chose (place, actors, goods, numbers before
→ after, the steps with their mechanism links, the naming sentence, the real-life link). Run that example FIRST, in beats that cover
the item and carry its numbers as digits ("dukaan mein chini ke 3 packet, ₹50 ka ek; kal 2 khareedar, aaj 12"), walking the mechanism
step by step (purpose story or example); only then the beat that names the term ("isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain"), then
the book's definition, then the real-life link. The opening question of such a topic asks about the situation, not the term. BIE's
code sends back a script whose naming beat comes before the example beats, or whose example beats carry none of the numbers.
Time (S2-01): the source gives this video's narration time; BIE's code counts the spoken words (130 a minute) and the script must stay
within it. Win the time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content: every item in must_cover is taught and every
teacher question whose basis is "book" is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the
time allows.
Prerequisites (S2-03): in a topic video they were already taught in the prerequisite video; remind of one in at most 2 beats (purpose
"prerequisite"). In the prerequisite video (card parts "pre1", "pre2" ...) teach each prerequisite simply, with an everyday example, in
the order given: part_id = the prerequisite id, step 0, covers_item_ids = the prerequisite ids the beat teaches, answers [].
A beat introduces at most a few new items: BIE's code measures the load of every beat (0.4 per new item plus 1 per 50 spoken words, at
most 1.8), so a beat holds at most about 70 spoken words with one new item, 50 with two and 30 with three; split longer beats. Reply
with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-27.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.
- Apply it in the real world first, then name it (Navin's sugar shop) (every economics concept (a definition, a cause-and-effect chain, a process): the example runs before the term is named): Ek kirana shop mein chini ke 3 packet hain, ₹50 ka ek. Kal 2 khareedar aaye the, aaj 12 aa gaye; sab ko chini chahiye par packet 3 hi hain. Dukandar daam ₹65 kar deta hai; ab sirf 3 log kharid paate hain, baaki 9 khaali haath. Zyada log, utna hi maal, isliye daam upar. Isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain. Phir book ki definition. Phir: yahi aap Diwali se pehle sabzi mandi mein dekhte hain.

Brackets (word list 2026-10-27.2): use everyday spoken Hindi freely, without brackets (मुख्य, वापस, बराबर, आसपास, इस्तेमाल, करके, जिससे ...). Only a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical) gets its English word in brackets right after it, for example "सतह (surface)", "घर्षण (friction)", "सघन (dense)"; better still, use the book's English term or a simpler Hindi word. Never put a bracket inside an idiom or a fixed phrase: "आम तौर पर", not "आम तौर (usually) पर"; "नहीं के बराबर", not "नहीं के बराबर (equal to)". BIE's code removes a bracket after an everyday word and asks for one only after a Hindi word it does not know as everyday.

Video v15: Money supply: M0 से M4 तक क्या गिना जाता है?
Goal: Learner aggregate overview से M0–M4 की पूरी family समझेगा; formulas को component by component बनाएगा और currency in circulation, public currency, RBI deposits, demand deposits, time deposits तथा post-office coverage की boundaries पहचान सकेगा।
Opening hook: जेब का cash, bank balance और fixed deposit—देश का money गिनते समय क्या सबको हर बार एक ही total में जोड़ेंगे?
Story or analogy: पहले अलग जगह रखी रकम की situation, फिर मापने की जरूरत और aggregate names आएँगे। Overview के बाद M0 का base अलग समझाएँगे; M1–M4 को component cards से बनाएँगे। M1–M2 और M3–M4 की direct comparison, liquidity, NSC exclusion और inclusion–exclusion checks होंगे; M0 को बाकी aggregates की सीधी nested सीढ़ी नहीं दिखाएँगे।
Planned minutes: 11
Narration time (S2-01): 9.0-12.0 minutes, about 1170-1560 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later; Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest; Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits; Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity; Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement; Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes; Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates; Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces

frame.when: Policy analysis compares monetary growth with credit, output and prices.
frame.conditions: M3 is an indicator, not proof of inflation; specific exclusions do not exclude all term deposits.
frame.atmosphere: A local business loan and a family's long-term savings decision.

beats.say: Wallet का cash, bank balance और FD दिख रहे हैं? Money गिनते समय क्या हमेशा सब जोड़ेंगे?
beats.on_screen: Wallet, bank balance and FD; question mark over total.

beats.say: खरीदार के ₹100, दुकानदार के ₹0 हैं। खरीदारी के बाद दोनों के balances उलट गए, लेकिन combined cash ₹100 ही रहा।
beats.on_screen: Buyer ₹100 → ₹0; shopkeeper ₹0 → ₹100; total unchanged.

beats.say: Money supply economy में एक तय पल पर spending, saving और payments के लिए उपलब्ध money है। Holdings की photo सोचो; यह stock है।
beats.on_screen: Freeze economy-wide holdings at one instant.

beats.say: महीने के payments का total यह stock नहीं है। वही ₹100 बार-बार इस्तेमाल हो सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Repeated payments with one ₹100 note versus one snapshot.

beats.say: यानी तय पल की holdings गिनेंगे। Cash और deposits इस्तेमाल करने की आसानी अलग है, इसलिए अलग measures चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Snapshot plus component boundary.

beats.say: Wallet और अलग accounts के पैसे कैसे गिनेंगे? RBI की aggregate family में M0, M1, M2, M3 और M4 हैं।
beats.on_screen: Five aggregate labels; M0 separate from M1-based branches.

beats.say: M0 reserve base, M1 payment-ready money है। M2 Post Office savings, M3 bank time deposits जोड़ता है; M4 wider Post Office coverage देता है।
beats.on_screen: Parallel cards: base, addition, coverage; M2 and M3 both start with M1.

beats.say: M2 और M3 दोनों M1 से बनते हैं, एक-दूसरे से नहीं। M3 important reporting measure है; M4 broadest है।
beats.on_screen: M1 branches to M2 and M3; distinguish importance from breadth.

beats.say: याद रखो: 0 base, 1 ready, 2 Post Office savings, 3 bank time, 4 wider coverage। Overlapping totals आपस में मत जोड़ना।
beats.on_screen: Memory strip; cross out sum of all aggregates.

beats.say: Pyramid नीचे चौड़ा होता दिख रहा है? इसकी 5 tiers M0 से M4 और deposit categories दिखाती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Five-tier white-outlined pyramid with no arrows.

beats.say: ऊपर सिर्फ M0 लिखा है। नीचे M1 में Cash + Demand Deposits है; यानी माँग पर निकल सकने वाला bank balance।
beats.on_screen: Highlight apex and M1 tier in order.

beats.say: M2 में + PO Savings Deposits है; PO यानी Post Office। M3 में + Bank Time Deposits है, जैसे FD।
beats.on_screen: Highlight M2 then M3; expand PO.

beats.say: M4 में + All PO Deposits, except NSC है। National Savings Certificates को बाहर रखना है।
beats.on_screen: Bottom tier highlighted; NSC outside.

beats.say: Plus देखकर पिछली tier मत जोड़ना: M0 अलग है, M3 का base M1 है। पूरी M1 formula में OD भी है।
beats.on_screen: Correct branches beside pyramid; OD added to full M1 definition.

beats.say: Picture से labels पहचानो, formulas से calculation करो। M2 सिर्फ Post Office savings जोड़ता है; M4 qualifying total, NSC नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Diagram for orientation; component baskets for calculation.

beats.say: किराने पर दिए ₹500 कहाँ गए? दुकानदार की sale receipt ₹0 से ₹500 हुई; उसने पैसे bank में जमा किए।
beats.on_screen: ₹500 household payment followed by shop deposit.

beats.say: यह money circulation है, यानी दुकान पर दिया पैसा आगे चलता है। Households, businesses और banks जुड़े हैं; banks का RBI से connection है।
beats.on_screen: Follow the shop payment into its bank; show a separate bank–RBI connection.

beats.say: Purchases, wages, deposits और loans पर पैसे चलते हैं। RBI transactions banks को जोड़ते हैं; हर खरीदारी सीधे RBI से नहीं गुजरती।
beats.on_screen: Animate payment paths and separate RBI transactions.

beats.say: Recipient अगला payment रोक दे तो आगे movement रुकेगा। पैसा गायब नहीं हुआ; अभी उसके पास है।
beats.on_screen: Pause next payment; balance stays with recipient.

beats.say: तेज़ी से चलाओ: खरीदार ने दिया, दुकानदार ने पाया और bank में जमा किया। पैसे रखने वाला और उसका form बदल गया।
beats.on_screen: Replay purchase and deposit.

beats.say: Circulation movement है; Money supply तय पल की holdings है। पैसा चलना हमेशा नया पैसा बनना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Flow versus stock.

beats.say: Bank का RBI balance कैसे बढ़े? RBI ₹100 की security खरीदकर credit करे, तो उसका balance ₹100 से ₹200 होगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical purchase; RBI account ₹100 → ₹200.

beats.say: सीधे RBI-created base M0 है: Reserve Money या High-Powered Money। Building के foundation जैसा, यह आगे bank money बनने का आधार है।
beats.on_screen: M0 foundation beneath bank deposits.

beats.say: तुम्हारा bank deposit सीधे M0 नहीं है। Bank का RBI balance अलग है; उससे withdrawals और दूसरे banks के payments सँभलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Customer account versus bank's RBI account.

beats.say: M0 monetary base है, सारे public deposits नहीं। यह lending को support करता है; lending अपने-आप नहीं होती।
beats.on_screen: Base supports, not guarantees, lending.

beats.say: Vault cash और bank का RBI balance कहाँ गिनेंगे? M0 में C, OD और Bankers' Deposits with RBI जोड़ते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Three M0 component boxes.

beats.say: Public cash ₹1000 और vault cash ₹200 से C ₹1200 है। Bank का RBI balance ₹800, OD zero हो तो M0 ₹2000 है।
beats.on_screen: Currency in circulation includes public and bank cash; total ₹2000.

beats.say: Bankers' Deposits में CRR balances शामिल हैं। Cash Reserve Ratio bank को RBI में तय हिस्सा रखने का नियम है; OD eligible दूसरे RBI deposits हैं।
beats.on_screen: CRR within bankers' deposits; OD separate; no numerical ratio assumed.

beats.say: Bank ₹100 notes ले तो vault ₹300, RBI balance ₹700 होगा। ₹1300 + ₹700 फिर ₹2000 हैं; customer bank deposits अलग claims हैं।
beats.on_screen: RBI balance moves to vault; M0 unchanged; customer account excluded.

beats.say: M0 = C + OD + Bankers' Deposits। C में public और bank cash हैं; accounts RBI में हैं। Date और unit एक रखो।
beats.on_screen: Build formula term by term.

beats.say: Loan से balance कैसे बढ़ता है? सारी ज़रूरी शर्तें पूरी मानो: Bank A ₹80 loan deposit बनाता है; borrower Bank B के supplier को देता है।
beats.on_screen: ₹80 loan creates deposit; supplier receives payment at Bank B.

beats.say: Bank B शर्तें पूरी करके ₹60 loan देता है। Repayments और cash leakage छोड़ें तो इन loans से नए deposits ₹0 से ₹140 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Second loan ₹60; illustrated new deposits total ₹140.

beats.say: यह reserves-supported multiple expansion है। Loan deposit बनाता है; banks के बीच payment settle करने के लिए reserve base चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Reserve support → lending → deposit → settlement.

beats.say: इसका दिखने वाला कदम account में loan credit है। Recipient पैसे bank में रखे तो system में deposits बने रहते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Loan-credit entry followed by recipient balance.

beats.say: Expansion guaranteed नहीं: withdrawals, reserve needs, capital, lending standards और loan demand इसे रोक सकते हैं। Bank बिना सीमा lending नहीं कर सकता।
beats.on_screen: Constraints gate further lending.

beats.say: Chain है: reserve support, loan deposit, payment settlement, फिर conditional lending। Multiple expansion पूरे banking system की बात है।
beats.on_screen: Complete conditional expansion chain.

beats.say: ₹200 का किराना अभी चाहिए? ₹500 cash से दोगे तो ₹300 बचेंगे; ₹1000 payment-ready account से ₹300 दो तो ₹700 बचेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Two separate immediate-payment examples.

beats.say: यह immediate-payment focus M1, Narrow Money की पहचान है। यह public का सबसे liquid money है, यानी जल्दी इस्तेमाल होने वाला पैसा।
beats.on_screen: M1: most liquid; almost immediately spendable.

beats.say: FD रखना अलग है; payment के लिए उसकी शर्तें आ सकती हैं। Narrow का मतलब तुरंत इस्तेमाल वाले components हैं, पतले notes नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Time deposits outside immediate-payment boundary.

beats.say: M1 में almost immediately spendable components गिनेंगे। अब formula से यह boundary साफ करेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Payment-ready boundary ready for component cards.

beats.say: Wallet और accounts कैसे जोड़ेंगे? M1 public currency, Demand Deposits और OD गिनता है; M2 Post Office savings जोड़कर Intermediate Money बनता है।
beats.on_screen: M1 components; M2 additional component.

beats.say: Hypothetical cash ₹1000, demand deposits ₹4000, OD zero: M1 contribution ₹5000 है। Post Office savings ₹2000 जोड़ो तो M2 ₹7000 है।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative contribution, not national totals: M1 ₹5000; M2 ₹7000.

beats.say: Demand deposits में on-demand current और savings balances आते हैं। M1 में bank vault cash और Bankers' Deposits नहीं; OD दोनों formulas में है।
beats.on_screen: M0 versus M1 inclusion table.

beats.say: ₹500 withdrawal से cash ₹1500, demand ₹3500: M1 ₹5000 रहा। Original balances से अलग ₹500 Post Office में डालो: ₹4500 + ₹2500, M2 ₹7000 रहा।
beats.on_screen: Independent reset examples; updated balances prevent double counting.

beats.say: M1 = public currency + Demand Deposits + OD। M2 = M1 + Post Office savings deposits; bank time deposits और NSC बाहर हैं।
beats.on_screen: Build both formulas; excluded cards remain outside.

beats.say: Post Office passbook और certificate दोनों जोड़ेंगे? M2 addition में savings-bank deposits included हैं; NSC और similar instruments excluded हैं।
beats.on_screen: Two-branch product classification.

beats.say: Savings deposit account balance है, इसलिए इस addition में आता है। NSC time-bound certificate है; institution वही हो, product अलग है।
beats.on_screen: Parallel product slots: form, access, institution, inclusion.

beats.say: Confused pair deposit और certificate है। सिर्फ Post Office लिखा देखकर दोनों को included मत मानना।
beats.on_screen: Deposit versus certificate.

beats.say: Trick रखो: M2 में eligible savings deposit, हर savings product नहीं। Exam में product पढ़ना है।
beats.on_screen: Memory cue: product, not just institution.

beats.say: दो accounts में पैसे हों तो इस्तेमाल उतना ही आसान होगा? Bank और Post Office savings दोनों में funds उपलब्ध हैं।
beats.on_screen: Shared availability of funds.

beats.say: Post Office savings fairly liquid हैं, लेकिन ordinary bank deposits से slightly less convenient हैं। इसका मतलब inaccessible नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Compare relative liquidity and convenience; no locked account.

beats.say: Funds उपलब्ध होना और access का रास्ता आसान होना अलग हैं। कोई खास present-day withdrawal restriction यहाँ नहीं मान रहे।
beats.on_screen: Availability versus access arrangements.

beats.say: Trap है less convenient को illiquid पढ़ना। तुलना पैसे मिलने की relative आसानी की है।
beats.on_screen: Less convenient ≠ inaccessible.

beats.say: याद रखो: Post Office savings fairly liquid, bank deposits से थोड़ी कम convenient। दोनों criteria अलग जाँचो।
beats.on_screen: Two-criterion comparison table.

beats.say: FD और recurring deposits कहाँ गिनेंगे? M3 Broad Money में आते हैं; यह important reporting measure है। M4 broadest है।
beats.on_screen: M3 importance versus M4 breadth.

beats.say: Broadest label अकेला formula नहीं बताता। M4 में M3 के बाहर के qualifying Post Office deposits भी हैं; यानी passbook वाला पैसा, सारी wealth नहीं। NSC बाहर है।
beats.on_screen: Breadth label first, component formula separately; include eligible passbook balances and exclude NSC.

beats.say: OD zero मानो: M1 ₹5000 और FD जैसे bank time deposits ₹6000 मिलकर M3 ₹11000 हैं। Post Office के ₹2000 savings और ₹3000 दूसरे eligible deposits से M4 ₹16000 है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical component cards: ₹5000 + ₹6000 = ₹11000; then + ₹2000 + ₹3000 = ₹16000. NSC remains outside.

beats.say: News का money supply growth आम तौर पर M3 है। इसमें FD, recurring यानी नियमित किस्तों वाले deposits, और दूसरे commercial-bank time deposits आते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Mock M3 headline; FD, RD and other time deposits.

beats.say: ₹1000 demand से FD में करो: demand ₹3000, time ₹7000। M1 ₹4000 हुआ; M3 ₹11000 रहा, क्योंकि दोनों components उसमें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Transfer within M3; M1 falls without broad-money creation.

beats.say: अलग snapshots में M3 ₹1000 crore स्थिर, eligible Post Office deposits ₹200 से ₹250 crore हों: M4 ₹1200 से ₹1250 crore होगा।
beats.on_screen: Same-date stocks per snapshot; common crore-rupee unit; NSC excluded.

beats.say: यह assumed accounting comparison है, transfer से money creation नहीं। Broadest coverage, important reporting और जमीन समेत total wealth अलग बातें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Breadth ≠ importance ≠ total wealth.

beats.say: M3 = M1 + bank time deposits, M2 नहीं। M4 = M3 + all qualifying Post Office deposits, excluding NSC; savings दोबारा मत जोड़ना।
beats.on_screen: Build formulas term by term; count eligible savings once.

beats.say: नया loan क्या बदलता है? ₹100 loan deposit बना, supplier ने bank में रखा; बाकी बदलाव न हों तो M3 ₹1000 से ₹1100 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: New lending increases illustrative M3 by ₹100.

beats.say: Certificate से किराना दोगे? ₹2000 cash में से ₹1000 का NSC खरीदो: cash ₹1000 बचेगा; खरीदारी में वही इस्तेमाल होगा, certificate नहीं।
पहला example RBI की M3 monitoring समझाता है। दूसरा NSC exclusion: वह long-term savings instrument है, readily spendable money नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Two reasoning tracks: monitoring and exclusion.

beats.say: M3 से liquidity और credit growth के संकेत मिलते हैं। यानी account balances और lending साथ जाँचेंगे; खरीदने की ताकत सामान से तेज़ बढ़े तो दामों पर दबाव बन सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Compare account balances and lending; then compare spending power with available goods, using a conditional price-pressure arrow.

beats.say: Policy effectiveness का check है: RBI के कदमों के बाद money, credit और prices चाही दिशा में गए? NSC लंबे समय की saving है, आज का payment balance नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Policy dashboard checks intended direction; separate long-term certificate from today's payment balance.

beats.say: News का M3 अकेला मत पढ़ो; credit और prices साथ जाँचो। Post Office product होना भी काफी नहीं: NSC बाहर है।
beats.on_screen: Read M3 alongside credit and prices; distinguish eligible deposits from NSC.

beats.say: M3 बढ़ना inflation का proof नहीं; यह loans का total भी नहीं। NSC बाहर होने से सारे long-term deposits बाहर नहीं होते।
beats.on_screen: Reject deterministic inflation and blanket long-term-deposit exclusion.

beats.say: RBI के checks हैं inflationary pressures, liquidity, credit growth और policy effectiveness। NSC long-term, readily spendable नहीं; इसलिए M4 से बाहर है।
beats.on_screen: Four monitoring gauges; NSC exclusion chain.

beats.say: Option जाँचो: किसका balance, कहाँ, कौन-सा product? M0 अलग base है; M2 और M3, M1 से बनते हैं। Form बदलना हमेशा money creation नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Final holder–institution–product checklist and correct aggregate map.

notes.about: This unit teaches the coverage and uses of M0–M4, separating reserve money from public-money aggregates. Its strongest feature is correcting the misleading cumulative interpretation of the pyramid.
key_questions: Which holdings enter each aggregate, and whose accounts are they?
Why can a transfer change narrow money without changing broad money?
Why does RBI monitor M3, while M4 has the widest coverage?
Why are NSCs excluded?

problems.problem: The maker supplies null rather than the required account of scope, decisions, reasons and uncertainties.
problems.fix: Populate the non-spoken notes, particularly explaining the pyramid correction, M3/M4 wording and hypothetical examples. No narration needs adding.

problems.problem: Aggregate names and formulas precede their numerical examples. The overview names the entire family before running its prescribed holdings example, and later sections again announce M0, M2 and M3 before calculation. Later examples do not restore the required example-first sequence.
problems.fix: Run the hypothetical holdings and transfers before naming the resulting aggregates. Reorder existing numerical beats ahead of definitions, and replace repeated overview/recap narration rather than adding runtime.

problems.problem: OD is explained only as 'eligible दूसरे RBI deposits'. This repeats the category without giving learners a concrete eligible holder or explaining the boundary. The claimed account-holder distinction therefore remains incomplete.
problems.fix: Replace part of the repeated M0 recap with a clearly labelled standard outside example, such as an IMF deposit at RBI, contrasted with a commercial bank's RBI account and a household's commercial-bank account. Clarify that not every other RBI balance automatically qualifies.

problems.problem: Time deposits are central to M3, but their agreed-term meaning and the reason for reduced payment readiness are never properly opened. b59 claims to answer p018-i12#q3 but only demonstrates a transfer and unchanged total.
problems.fix: Before naming time deposits, describe money placed until an agreed date and conditional premature access, then connect this to FD and recurring deposits. Replace repeated importance/breadth narration or the duplicate final recap to make room.

problems.problem: The comparison repeatedly states 'fairly liquid but less convenient' without a concrete access situation explaining the difference. 'Access का रास्ता आसान होना' paraphrases the distinction rather than opening its mechanism.
problems.fix: Replace one repeated comparison and trap beat with a hypothetical equal-balance payment situation showing funds being available but requiring an additional access step. Explicitly avoid presenting that illustration as a current universal restriction.

'Access का रास्ता आसान होना' paraphrases the distinction rather than opening its mechanism. -> fix: Replace one repeated comparison and trap beat with a hypothetical equal-balance payment situation showing funds being available but requiring an additional access step. Explicitly avoid presenting that illustration as a current universal restriction.

frame.process: Define the economy's money holdings at an instant.
frame.how: Transfer ₹100 between two holders, then distinguish the unchanged stock from payments.
frame.when: Measure at one selected instant, not across a month.
frame.conditions: Specify eligible monetary components and avoid repeated counting.
frame.atmosphere: A buyer pays a neighbourhood kirana shop.

frame.process: Organize the five aggregate names by coverage.
frame.how: Keep M0 separate; branch M2 and M3 from M1 and extend M3 to M4.
frame.when: Overview precedes detailed formulas.
frame.conditions: Overlapping aggregates must not be added together.
frame.atmosphere: A household and shop hold cash and several kinds of deposits.

frame.process: Read and qualify the five-tier money pyramid.
frame.how: Scan apex to base, then replace misleading cumulative implications with component baskets.
frame.when: After the family overview and before detailed mechanisms.
frame.conditions: Printed abbreviations are not complete definitions.
frame.atmosphere: Five widening tiers beside an accurate branch diagram.

frame.process: Money moves through payments and deposits.
frame.how: Follow a household payment to a shop and its bank, with a separate bank–RBI link.
frame.when: During purchases, wages, deposits and lending.
frame.conditions: A payment generally transfers money; every household payment need not directly involve RBI.
frame.atmosphere: A local shop connected to the banking system.

frame.process: Identify directly RBI-created reserve money.
frame.how: An RBI security purchase credits a bank's reserve account.
frame.when: Central-bank money provides a base for subsequent banking activity.
frame.conditions: Reserves support settlement and potential lending, not compulsory lending.
frame.atmosphere: RBI and a commercial bank's reserve account.

frame.process: Construct M0 from three monetary stocks.
frame.how: Distinguish circulating currency, other RBI deposits and bankers' RBI deposits.
frame.when: Use balances for the same instant.
frame.conditions: Use common units; include bank vault cash and CRR balances without double counting.
frame.atmosphere: Public wallets, a bank vault and accounts held at RBI.

frame.process: Bank lending creates deposit money across the banking system.
frame.how: An ₹80 loan and a subsequent ₹60 loan create ₹140 of deposits under stated assumptions.
frame.when: Lending and interbank settlement occur in successive rounds.
frame.conditions: Reserves, capital, liquidity, lending standards and credit demand constrain expansion.
frame.atmosphere: Two banks, a business borrower and a supplier.

frame.process: Define M1 through near-immediate spendability.
frame.how: Demonstrate a cash purchase and a demand-account payment before explaining Narrow Money.
frame.when: Funds are needed for everyday transactions.
frame.conditions: Almost immediate use does not mean every form of savings qualifies.
frame.atmosphere: A customer paying for groceries.

frame.process: Build M1 and M2 component by component.
frame.how: Add public currency, demand deposits and other RBI deposits; then add eligible post-office savings deposits.
frame.when: Compare updated balances after completed transfers.
frame.conditions: Exclude bank vault cash from public currency and NSC from the M2 addition.
frame.atmosphere: Wallet, bank account and post-office passbook.

frame.process: Classify post-office products as included or excluded in the M2 addition.
frame.how: Separate savings-bank deposits from NSC and similar instruments.
frame.when: Before adding post-office holdings to M1.
frame.conditions: Product type, not the institution alone, determines inclusion.
frame.atmosphere: Two different savings products offered at a post office.

frame.process: Compare liquidity and convenience of savings deposits.
frame.how: Contrast availability of funds with ease of accessing or using them.
frame.when: A saver needs money for a payment.
frame.conditions: Relative inconvenience does not imply inaccessibility; no current restrictions are assumed.
frame.atmosphere: A saver comparing bank and post-office account access.

frame.process: Construct M3 and M4 and distinguish importance from breadth.
frame.how: Add bank time deposits to M1, then qualifying post-office deposits to M3.
frame.when: Use same-date stocks; reset assumptions for separate worked examples.
frame.conditions: M3 does not start from M2; M4 excludes NSC and counts post-office savings once.
frame.atmosphere: A bank FD conversion, a monetary-statistics desk and a news headline.

frame.process: Explain RBI monitoring and the NSC exclusion.
frame.how: Trace loan-created deposits into monetary indicators, then contrast spendable cash with a long-term certificate.
frame.when: Policy analysis compares monetary growth with credit, output and prices.
frame.conditions: M3 is an indicator, not proof of inflation; specific exclusions do not exclude all term deposits.
frame.atmosphere: A local business loan and a family's long-term savings decision.

beats.on_screen: Buyer ₹100 → ₹0; shopkeeper ₹0 → ₹100; total unchanged.

beats.on_screen: Freeze economy-wide holdings at one instant.

beats.say: महीने के payments का total यह stock नहीं है। वही ₹100 बार-बार इस्तेमाल हो सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Repeated payments with one ₹100 note versus one snapshot.

beats.on_screen: Snapshot plus component boundary.

beats.say: M2 में + PO Savings Deposits है; PO यानी Post Office। M3 में + Bank Time Deposits है, जैसे FD।

beats.say: M0 monetary base है, सारे public deposits नहीं। यह lending को support करता है; lending अपने-आप नहीं होती।
beats.on_screen: Base supports, not guarantees, lending.

beats.say: Public cash ₹1000, vault cash ₹200 और bank का RBI balance ₹800 हो तो कितना base पैसा है? Other RBI deposits zero मानकर total ₹2000 है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical monetary-base holdings: ₹1000 + ₹200 + ₹800 = ₹2000; no formula labels yet.

beats.say: Bank RBI account से ₹100 notes ले: vault ₹300, RBI balance ₹700। Total फिर ₹2000 है; public cash नहीं बढ़ा। यही M0 की composition बदलना है।
beats.on_screen: Currency in circulation ₹1200 → ₹1300; bankers' RBI deposits ₹800 → ₹700; M0 ₹2000 unchanged.

beats.say: C यानी Currency in circulation में public और bank cash हैं। Bankers' Deposits में CRR balances भी हैं; Cash Reserve Ratio relevant bank liabilities का RBI में रखा जाने वाला तय हिस्सा है।
beats.on_screen: C spans wallets and vault. Bankers' Deposits with RBI includes CRR; no numerical ratio supplied.

beats.say: OD का standard outside example IMF का RBI deposit है। Commercial bank का RBI account Bankers' Deposits है; तुम्हारा commercial-bank account दोनों नहीं। हर दूसरा RBI balance अपने-आप OD नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Label outside example: IMF = International Monetary Fund. Compare holder, account institution and category in three rows; household account is a commercial-bank liability, not an RBI liability.

beats.say: अब formula बनाओ: M0 = C + OD + Bankers' Deposits। तीनों same-date stocks, एक unit में जोड़ो; customer deposits इसमें मत डालना।
beats.on_screen: Build formula from the three explained boxes; common date and monetary unit.

beats.say: Loan से balance कैसे बढ़ता है? सारी ज़रूरी शर्तें पूरी मानो: Bank A ₹80 loan deposit बनाता है; borrower Bank B के supplier को देता है।
beats.on_screen: ₹80 loan creates deposit; supplier receives payment at Bank B.

beats.say: Bank B शर्तें पूरी करके ₹60 loan देता है। Repayments और cash leakage छोड़ें तो इन loans से नए deposits ₹0 से ₹140 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Second loan ₹60; illustrated new deposits total ₹140.

beats.say: यह reserves-supported multiple expansion है। Loan deposit बनाता है; banks के बीच payment settle करने के लिए reserve base चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Reserve support → lending → deposit → settlement.

beats.say: इसका दिखने वाला कदम account में loan credit है। Recipient पैसे bank में रखे तो system में deposits बने रहते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Loan-credit entry followed by recipient balance.

beats.say: Expansion guaranteed नहीं: withdrawals, reserve needs, capital, lending standards और loan demand इसे रोक सकते हैं। Bank बिना सीमा lending नहीं कर सकता।
beats.on_screen: Constraints gate further lending.

beats.say: Chain है: reserve support, loan deposit, payment settlement, फिर conditional lending। Multiple expansion पूरे banking system की बात है।
beats.on_screen: Complete conditional expansion chain.

beats.say: ₹200 का किराना अभी चाहिए? ₹500 cash से दोगे तो ₹300 बचेंगे; ₹1000 payment-ready account से ₹300 दो तो ₹700 बचेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Two separate immediate-payment examples.

beats.say: यह immediate-payment focus M1, Narrow Money की पहचान है। यह public का सबसे liquid money है, यानी जल्दी इस्तेमाल होने वाला पैसा।
beats.on_screen: M1: most liquid; almost immediately spendable.

beats.say: FD रखना अलग है; payment के लिए उसकी शर्तें आ सकती हैं। Narrow का मतलब तुरंत इस्तेमाल वाले components हैं, पतले notes नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Time deposits outside immediate-payment boundary.

beats.say: M1 में almost immediately spendable components गिनेंगे। अब formula से यह boundary साफ करेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Payment-ready boundary ready for component cards.

beats.say: Cash ₹1000, demand balance ₹4000 और other RBI deposits zero हों तो ₹5000 हुए। Post Office savings ₹2000 भी गिनें तो ₹7000 होंगे; किस boundary में क्या आएगा?
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical contribution, not national totals. Calculate ₹5000 and ₹7000 before revealing aggregate labels.

beats.say: ₹500 cash Post Office savings में रखो: cash ₹500, savings ₹2500 हुए। ₹4500 + ₹2500 फिर ₹7000 हैं। इस wider total को M2, Intermediate Money कहते हैं; इसका base M1 है।
beats.on_screen: Completed hypothetical transfer, no offsetting changes. M1 contribution ₹5000 → ₹4500; M2 ₹7000 unchanged. Reveal M2 name after arithmetic.

beats.say: Demand deposits में on-demand current और savings balances आते हैं। M1 में bank vault cash और Bankers' Deposits नहीं; OD दोनों formulas में है।
beats.on_screen: M0 versus M1 inclusion table.

beats.say: Original balances पर लौटो। Bank से ₹500 निकालो तो cash ₹1500, demand ₹3500: M1 ₹5000 रहा। Account की पुरानी रकम फिर जोड़ोगे तो double counting होगी।
beats.on_screen: Reset original cash ₹1000 and demand ₹4000; withdraw ₹500; sum updated balances only.

beats.say: M1 = public currency + Demand Deposits + OD। M2 = M1 + Post Office savings deposits; bank time deposits और NSC बाहर हैं।
beats.on_screen: Build both formulas; excluded cards remain outside.

beats.say: Post Office passbook और certificate दोनों जोड़ेंगे? M2 addition में savings-bank deposits included हैं; NSC और similar instruments excluded हैं।
beats.on_screen: Two-branch product classification.

beats.say: Savings deposit account balance है, इसलिए इस addition में आता है। NSC time-bound certificate है; institution वही हो, product अलग है।
beats.on_screen: Parallel product slots: form, access, institution, inclusion.

beats.say: Confused pair deposit और certificate है। सिर्फ Post Office लिखा देखकर दोनों को included मत मानना।
beats.on_screen: Deposit versus certificate.

beats.say: Trick रखो: M2 में eligible savings deposit, हर savings product नहीं। Exam में product पढ़ना है।
beats.on_screen: Memory cue: product, not just institution.

beats.say: दो accounts में ₹1000 हों तो ₹300 का bill देना बराबर आसान होगा? दोनों में रकम है; अब इस्तेमाल का रास्ता देखो।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical equal balances: ordinary bank deposit ₹1000 and PO savings ₹1000; grocery bill ₹300.

beats.say: मानो bank account से bill सीधे दे सकते हो, लेकिन चुने गए Post Office access में पहले cash निकालना पड़े। पैसे दोनों जगह हैं; दूसरे रास्ते में 1 extra step है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration only: bank account → ₹300 payment; selected PO access → cash withdrawal → ₹300 payment. Not a universal current restriction.

beats.say: यह सिर्फ illustration है, आज का universal restriction नहीं। रकम निकाल सकना liquidity है; उसे payment तक पहुँचाने के steps convenience बदलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Separate fund availability from access steps; hypothetical qualification stays visible.

beats.say: इसलिए fairly liquid और slightly less convenient साथ हो सकते हैं। Less convenient का मतलब पैसे inaccessible होना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Confused pair: less convenient ≠ inaccessible.

beats.say: तुलना याद रखो: Post Office savings fairly liquid, ordinary bank deposits से थोड़ी कम convenient हैं। Availability और access अलग जाँचो।
beats.on_screen: Two-row recap table: liquidity and relative convenience.

beats.say: Account से ₹1000 agreed date तक अलग रखो तो payment-ready रकम क्या होगी? जल्दी निकालने पर शर्तें हो सकती हैं। ऐसी bank रकम Time Deposits है; FD और recurring deposits इसके examples हैं।
beats.on_screen: Demand account transfers ₹1000 into an agreed-term holding. Conditional premature access; reveal Time Deposits, FD and recurring deposits after the situation.

beats.say: याद रखो, widest coverage और सबसे इस्तेमाल होने वाला measure अलग बातें हैं। सिर्फ broadest label से components नहीं मिलते; अब eligible balances जोड़कर देखो।
beats.on_screen: Coverage versus reporting importance; leave aggregate-result labels hidden until calculation.

beats.say: M1 ₹5000 में bank time deposits ₹6000 जोड़ो: ₹11000, यानी M3 या Broad Money। फिर Post Office savings ₹2000 और दूसरे eligible deposits ₹3000 जोड़ो: ₹16000, यानी M4; NSC बाहर है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical contributions, OD zero. Calculate before revealing M3 and M4 labels; NSC card excluded. PO savings counted once.

beats.say: M3 important money-supply measure है; news में growth आम तौर पर इसी की होती है। M4 broadest है। Recurring deposits यानी नियमित किस्तों की बचत भी bank time deposits में आती है।
beats.on_screen: Mock M3 growth headline; M3 importance versus M4 breadth; FD, RD and other bank time deposits.

beats.say: ₹1000 demand से FD में करो: demand ₹3000, time ₹7000। M1 ₹4000 हुआ; M3 ₹11000 रहा, क्योंकि दोनों components उसमें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Reset original hypothetical holdings. Demand ₹4000 → ₹3000; time ₹6000 → ₹7000; M3 unchanged.

beats.say: अलग snapshots में M3 ₹1000 crore स्थिर, eligible Post Office deposits ₹200 से ₹250 crore हों: M4 ₹1200 से ₹1250 crore होगा।
beats.on_screen: Same-date stocks per snapshot; common crore-rupee unit; NSC excluded.

beats.say: यह assumed accounting comparison है, transfer से money creation नहीं। Broadest coverage, important reporting और जमीन समेत total wealth अलग बातें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Breadth ≠ importance ≠ total wealth.

beats.say: M3 = M1 + bank time deposits, M2 नहीं। M4 = M3 + all qualifying Post Office deposits, excluding NSC; savings दोबारा मत जोड़ना।
beats.on_screen: Build formulas term by term; count eligible savings once.

beats.say: नया loan क्या बदलता है? ₹100 loan deposit बना, supplier ने bank में रखा; बाकी बदलाव न हों तो M3 ₹1000 से ₹1100 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: New lending increases illustrative M3 by ₹100.

beats.say: Certificate से किराना दोगे? ₹2000 cash में से ₹1000 का NSC खरीदो: cash ₹1000 बचेगा; खरीदारी में वही इस्तेमाल होगा, certificate नहीं।
पहला example RBI की M3 monitoring समझाता है। दूसरा NSC exclusion: वह long-term savings instrument है, readily spendable money नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Two reasoning tracks: monitoring and exclusion.

beats.say: M3 से liquidity और credit growth के संकेत मिलते हैं। यानी account balances और lending साथ जाँचेंगे; खरीदने की ताकत सामान से तेज़ बढ़े तो दामों पर दबाव बन सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Compare account balances and lending; then compare spending power with available goods, using a conditional price-pressure arrow.

beats.say: Policy effectiveness का check है: RBI के कदमों के बाद money, credit और prices चाही दिशा में गए? NSC लंबे समय की saving है, आज का payment balance नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Policy dashboard checks intended direction; separate long-term certificate from today's payment balance.

beats.say: News का M3 अकेला मत पढ़ो; credit और prices साथ जाँचो। Post Office product होना भी काफी नहीं: NSC बाहर है।
beats.on_screen: Read M3 alongside credit and prices; distinguish eligible deposits from NSC.

beats.say: M3 बढ़ना inflation का proof नहीं; यह loans का total भी नहीं। NSC बाहर होने से सारे long-term deposits बाहर नहीं होते।
beats.on_screen: Reject deterministic inflation and blanket long-term-deposit exclusion.

beats.say: RBI के checks हैं inflationary pressures, liquidity, credit growth और policy effectiveness। NSC long-term, readily spendable नहीं; इसलिए M4 से बाहर है।
beats.on_screen: Four monitoring gauges; NSC exclusion chain.

beats.say: Option जाँचो: किसका balance, कहाँ, कौन-सा product? M0 अलग base है; M2 और M3, M1 से बनते हैं। Form बदलना हमेशा money creation नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Final holder–institution–product checklist and correct aggregate map.

frame.process: Define the economy's money holdings at an instant.
frame.how: Transfer ₹100 between two holders, then distinguish the unchanged stock from payments.
frame.when: Measure at one selected instant, not across a month.
frame.conditions: Specify eligible monetary components and avoid repeated counting.
frame.atmosphere: A buyer pays a neighbourhood kirana shop.

frame.process: Organize the five aggregate names by coverage.
frame.how: Keep M0 separate; branch M2 and M3 from M1 and extend M3 to M4.
frame.when: Overview precedes detailed formulas.
frame.conditions: Overlapping aggregates must not be added together.
frame.atmosphere: A household and shop hold cash and several kinds of deposits.

frame.process: Read and qualify the five-tier money pyramid.
frame.how: Scan apex to base, then replace misleading cumulative implications with component baskets.
frame.when: After the family overview and before detailed mechanisms.
frame.conditions: Printed abbreviations are not complete definitions.
frame.atmosphere: Five widening tiers beside an accurate branch diagram.

frame.process: Money moves through payments and deposits.
frame.how: Follow a household payment to a shop and its bank, with a separate bank–RBI link.
frame.when: During purchases, wages, deposits and lending.
frame.conditions: A payment generally transfers money; every household payment need not directly involve RBI.
frame.atmosphere: A local shop connected to the banking system.

frame.process: Identify directly RBI-created reserve money.
frame.how: An RBI security purchase credits a bank's reserve account.
frame.when: Central-bank money provides a base for subsequent banking activity.
frame.conditions: Reserves support settlement and potential lending, not compulsory lending.
frame.atmosphere: RBI and a commercial bank's reserve account.

frame.process: Construct M0 from three monetary stocks.
frame.how: Distinguish circulating currency, other RBI deposits and bankers' RBI deposits.
frame.when: Use balances for the same instant.
frame.conditions: Use common units; include bank vault cash and CRR balances without double counting.
frame.atmosphere: Public wallets, a bank vault and accounts held at RBI.

frame.process: Bank lending creates deposit money across the banking system.
frame.how: An ₹80 loan and a subsequent ₹60 loan create ₹140 of deposits under stated assumptions.
frame.when: Lending and interbank settlement occur in successive rounds.
frame.conditions: Reserves, capital, liquidity, lending standards and credit demand constrain expansion.
frame.atmosphere: Two banks, a business borrower and a supplier.

frame.process: Define M1 through near-immediate spendability.
frame.how: Demonstrate a cash purchase and a demand-account payment before explaining Narrow Money.
frame.when: Funds are needed for everyday transactions.
frame.conditions: Almost immediate use does not mean every form of savings qualifies.
frame.atmosphere: A customer paying for groceries.

frame.process: Build M1 and M2 component by component.
frame.how: Add public currency, demand deposits and other RBI deposits; then add eligible post-office savings deposits.
frame.when: Compare updated balances after completed transfers.
frame.conditions: Exclude bank vault cash from public currency and NSC from the M2 addition.
frame.atmosphere: Wallet, bank account and post-office passbook.

frame.process: Classify post-office products as included or excluded in the M2 addition.
frame.how: Separate savings-bank deposits from NSC and similar instruments.
frame.when: Before adding post-office holdings to M1.
frame.conditions: Product type, not the institution alone, determines inclusion.
frame.atmosphere: Two different savings products offered at a post office.

frame.process: Compare liquidity and convenience of savings deposits.
frame.how: Contrast availability of funds with ease of accessing or using them.
frame.when: A saver needs money for a payment.
frame.conditions: Relative inconvenience does not imply inaccessibility; no current restrictions are assumed.
frame.atmosphere: A saver comparing bank and post-office account access.

frame.process: Construct M3 and M4 and distinguish importance from breadth.
frame.how: Add bank time deposits to M1, then qualifying post-office deposits to M3.
frame.when: Use same-date stocks; reset assumptions for separate worked examples.
frame.conditions: M3 does not start from M2; M4 excludes NSC and counts post-office savings once.
frame.atmosphere: A bank FD conversion, a monetary-statistics desk and a news headline.

frame.process: Explain RBI monitoring and the NSC exclusion.
frame.how: Trace loan-created deposits into monetary indicators, then contrast spendable cash with a long-term certificate.
frame.when: Policy analysis compares monetary growth with credit, output and prices.
frame.conditions: M3 is an indicator, not proof of inflation; specific exclusions do not exclude all term deposits.
frame.atmosphere: A local business loan and a family's long-term savings decision.

beats.say: Wallet का cash, bank balance और FD दिख रहे हैं? Money गिनते समय क्या हमेशा सब जोड़ेंगे?
beats.on_screen: Wallet, bank balance and FD; question mark over total.

beats.say: खरीदार के ₹100, दुकानदार के ₹0 हैं। खरीदारी के बाद दोनों के balances उलट गए, लेकिन combined cash ₹100 ही रहा।
beats.on_screen: Buyer ₹100 → ₹0; shopkeeper ₹0 → ₹100; total unchanged.

beats.say: Money supply economy में एक तय पल पर spending, saving और payments के लिए उपलब्ध money है। Holdings की photo सोचो; यह stock है।
beats.on_screen: Freeze economy-wide holdings at one instant.

beats.say: महीने के payments का total यह stock नहीं है। वही ₹100 बार-बार इस्तेमाल हो सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Repeated payments with one ₹100 note versus one snapshot.

beats.say: यानी तय पल की holdings गिनेंगे। Cash और deposits इस्तेमाल करने की आसानी अलग है, इसलिए अलग measures चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Snapshot plus component boundary.

beats.say: अलग holdings कैसे गिनोगे? Hypothetical cash ₹1000, demand account ₹4000, bank में तय समय की रकम ₹6000, Post Office savings ₹2000 और दूसरे eligible deposits ₹3000 लो; RBI के other deposits zero मानो।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical holdings cards; separate excluded NSC ₹5000 card. Cash plus demand ₹5000; add PO savings ₹7000; alternatively add bank term holdings ₹11000; add qualifying PO total ₹16000. Do not yet label totals with aggregate names.

beats.say: Cash और demand ₹5000 हैं; Post Office savings के साथ ₹7000। ₹5000 में bank की ₹6000 जोड़ो: ₹11000; फिर Post Office की ₹5000 जोड़ो: ₹16000। ये M1, M2, M3, M4 हैं; M0 अलग reserve base है।
beats.on_screen: Reveal M1 ₹5000, M2 ₹7000, M3 ₹11000 and M4 ₹16000 after calculations. M0 separate; M2 and M3 branch from M1. NSC excluded.

beats.say: अब demand से ₹1000 तय समय की deposit में रखो: balances ₹3000 और ₹7000 हुए। M1 ₹4000, M2 ₹6000 हुए; M3 ₹11000 और M4 ₹16000 रहे। इसलिए M2 और M3 की additions अलग समझो।
beats.on_screen: Transfer ₹1000 between demand and term columns. Before/after four-total table; no new money created.

beats.say: याद रखो: M0 base; M2 Post Office savings, M3 bank time जोड़ता है। M3 important reporting measure, M4 broadest है। Overlapping totals मत जोड़ना।
beats.on_screen: Memory branches from M1; M0 separate. M3 importance versus M4 breadth. Cross out sum of aggregates.

beats.say: Pyramid नीचे चौड़ा होता दिख रहा है? इसकी 5 tiers M0 से M4 और deposit categories दिखाती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Five-tier white-outlined pyramid with no arrows.

beats.say: ऊपर सिर्फ M0 लिखा है। नीचे M1 में Cash + Demand Deposits है; यानी माँग पर निकल सकने वाला bank balance।
beats.on_screen: Highlight apex and M1 tier in order.

beats.say: M2 में + PO Savings Deposits है; PO यानी Post Office। M3 में + Bank Time Deposits है, जैसे FD।
beats.on_screen: Highlight M2 then M3; expand PO.

beats.say: M4 में + All PO Deposits, except NSC है। National Savings Certificates को बाहर रखना है।
beats.on_screen: Bottom tier highlighted; NSC outside.

beats.say: Plus देखकर पिछली tier मत जोड़ना: M0 अलग है, M3 का base M1 है। पूरी M1 formula में OD भी है।
beats.on_screen: Correct branches beside pyramid; OD added to full M1 definition.

beats.say: Picture से labels पहचानो, formulas से calculation करो। M2 सिर्फ Post Office savings जोड़ता है; M4 qualifying total, NSC नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Diagram for orientation; component baskets for calculation.

beats.say: किराने पर दिए ₹500 कहाँ गए? दुकानदार की sale receipt ₹0 से ₹500 हुई; उसने पैसे bank में जमा किए।
beats.on_screen: ₹500 household payment followed by shop deposit.

beats.say: यह money circulation है, यानी दुकान पर दिया पैसा आगे चलता है। Households, businesses और banks जुड़े हैं; banks का RBI से connection है।
beats.on_screen: Follow the shop payment into its bank; show a separate bank–RBI connection.

beats.say: Purchases, wages, deposits और loans पर पैसे चलते हैं। RBI transactions banks को जोड़ते हैं; हर खरीदारी सीधे RBI से नहीं गुजरती।
beats.on_screen: Animate payment paths and separate RBI transactions.

beats.say: Recipient अगला payment रोक दे तो आगे movement रुकेगा। पैसा गायब नहीं हुआ; अभी उसके पास है।
beats.on_screen: Pause next payment; balance stays with recipient.

beats.say: फिर चलाओ: खरीदार ने दिया, दुकानदार ने bank में जमा किया। Holder और form बदले।
beats.on_screen: Replay purchase and bank deposit.

beats.say: Circulation movement है; Money supply तय पल की holdings है। पैसा चलना हमेशा नया पैसा बनना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Flow versus stock.

beats.say: Bank का RBI balance कैसे बढ़े? RBI ₹100 की security खरीदकर credit करे, तो उसका balance ₹100 से ₹200 होगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical purchase; RBI account ₹100 → ₹200.

beats.say: सीधे RBI-created base M0 है: Reserve Money या High-Powered Money। Building के foundation जैसा, यह आगे bank money बनने का आधार है।
beats.on_screen: M0 foundation beneath bank deposits.

beats.say: तुम्हारा deposit M0 नहीं। Bank का RBI balance अलग है; यह withdrawals और interbank payments सँभालता है।
beats.on_screen: Customer deposit versus bank's RBI balance.

beats.say: M0 base है, public deposits नहीं; lending को support करता है, मजबूर नहीं करता।
beats.on_screen: Reserve base supports conditional lending.

beats.say: Public cash ₹1000, vault cash ₹200 और bank का RBI balance ₹800 हो तो कितना base पैसा है? Other RBI deposits zero मानकर total ₹2000 है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical monetary-base holdings: ₹1000 + ₹200 + ₹800 = ₹2000; no formula labels yet.

beats.say: Bank RBI account से ₹100 के notes लेता है। Vault cash ₹300 और RBI balance ₹700 हो जाता है। M0 ₹2000 रहता है; public cash नहीं बढ़ता।
beats.on_screen: Currency in circulation ₹1200 → ₹1300; bankers' RBI deposits ₹800 → ₹700; M0 unchanged at ₹2000.

beats.say: C यानी Currency in circulation में public और bank cash हैं। Bankers' Deposits में CRR balances भी हैं; Cash Reserve Ratio relevant bank liabilities का RBI में रखा जाने वाला तय हिस्सा है।
beats.on_screen: C spans wallets and vault. Bankers' Deposits with RBI includes CRR; no numerical ratio supplied.

beats.say: OD का standard outside example IMF का RBI deposit है। Commercial bank का RBI account Bankers' Deposits है; तुम्हारा commercial-bank account दोनों नहीं। हर दूसरा RBI balance अपने-आप OD नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Label outside example: IMF = International Monetary Fund. Compare holder, account institution and category in three rows; household account is a commercial-bank liability, not an RBI liability.

beats.say: अब formula बनाओ: M0 = C + OD + Bankers' Deposits। तीनों same-date stocks, एक unit में जोड़ो; customer deposits इसमें मत डालना।
beats.on_screen: Build formula from the three explained boxes; common date and monetary unit.

beats.say: Loan से balance कैसे बढ़ता है? सारी ज़रूरी शर्तें पूरी मानो: Bank A ₹80 loan deposit बनाता है; borrower Bank B के supplier को देता है।
beats.on_screen: ₹80 loan creates deposit; supplier receives payment at Bank B.

beats.say: Bank B शर्तें पूरी करके ₹60 loan देता है। Repayments और cash leakage छोड़ें तो इन loans से नए deposits ₹0 से ₹140 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Second loan ₹60; illustrated new deposits total ₹140.

beats.say: यह reserves-supported multiple expansion है। Loan deposit बनाता है; banks के बीच payment settle करने के लिए reserve base चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Reserve support → lending → deposit → settlement.

beats.say: Account में loan credit देखो। Recipient पैसे bank में रखे तो deposits system में रहते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Loan credit followed by recipient's bank balance.

beats.say: Expansion guaranteed नहीं: withdrawals, reserve needs, capital, lending standards और loan demand इसे रोक सकते हैं। Bank बिना सीमा lending नहीं कर सकता।
beats.on_screen: Constraints gate further lending.

beats.say: Reserve support से loan deposit, settlement और conditional lending होती है। Expansion पूरे banking system में है।
beats.on_screen: Reserve support → loan deposit → settlement → conditional further lending.

beats.say: ₹200 का किराना अभी चाहिए? ₹500 cash से दोगे तो ₹300 बचेंगे; ₹1000 payment-ready account से ₹300 दो तो ₹700 बचेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Two separate immediate-payment examples.

beats.say: यह immediate-payment focus M1, Narrow Money की पहचान है। यह public का सबसे liquid money है, यानी जल्दी इस्तेमाल होने वाला पैसा।
beats.on_screen: M1: most liquid; almost immediately spendable.

beats.say: FD में access की शर्तें हो सकती हैं। Narrow तुरंत इस्तेमाल वाले components हैं, पतले notes नहीं।
beats.on_screen: FD outside immediate-payment boundary.

beats.say: M1 almost immediately spendable components गिनता है। अब formula बनाओ।
beats.on_screen: Payment-ready components become formula cards.

beats.say: Cash ₹1000, demand balance ₹4000 और other RBI deposits zero हों तो ₹5000 हुए। Post Office savings ₹2000 भी गिनें तो ₹7000 होंगे; किस boundary में क्या आएगा?
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical contribution, not national totals. Calculate ₹5000 and ₹7000 before revealing aggregate labels.

beats.say: ₹500 cash Post Office savings में रखो: cash ₹500, savings ₹2500 हुए। ₹4500 + ₹2500 फिर ₹7000 हैं। इस wider total को M2, Intermediate Money कहते हैं; इसका base M1 है।
beats.on_screen: Completed hypothetical transfer, no offsetting changes. M1 contribution ₹5000 → ₹4500; M2 ₹7000 unchanged. Reveal M2 name after arithmetic.

beats.say: Demand deposits में on-demand current और savings balances आते हैं। M1 में bank vault cash और Bankers' Deposits नहीं; OD दोनों formulas में है।
beats.on_screen: M0 versus M1 inclusion table.

beats.say: Original balances पर लौटो। Bank से ₹500 निकालो तो cash ₹1500, demand ₹3500: M1 ₹5000 रहा। Account की पुरानी रकम फिर जोड़ोगे तो double counting होगी।
beats.on_screen: Reset original cash ₹1000 and demand ₹4000; withdraw ₹500; sum updated balances only.

beats.say: M1 = public currency + Demand Deposits + OD। M2 = M1 + Post Office savings deposits; bank time deposits और NSC बाहर हैं।
beats.on_screen: Build both formulas; excluded cards remain outside.

beats.say: Post Office passbook और certificate दोनों जोड़ेंगे? M2 addition में savings-bank deposits included हैं; NSC और similar instruments excluded हैं।
beats.on_screen: Two-branch product classification.

beats.say: Savings deposit account balance है, इसलिए इस addition में आता है। NSC time-bound certificate है; institution वही हो, product अलग है।
beats.on_screen: Parallel product slots: form, access, institution, inclusion.

beats.say: Deposit और certificate अलग हैं; Post Office नाम देखकर दोनों मत जोड़ना।
beats.on_screen: Deposit included; certificate excluded.

beats.say: Exam trick: M2 में eligible savings deposit है, हर savings product नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Read product type, not merely institution.

beats.say: दो accounts में ₹1000 हों तो ₹300 का bill देना बराबर आसान होगा? दोनों में रकम है; अब इस्तेमाल का रास्ता देखो।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical equal balances: ordinary bank deposit ₹1000 and PO savings ₹1000; grocery bill ₹300.

beats.say: मानो bank account से bill सीधे दे सकते हो, लेकिन चुने गए Post Office access में पहले cash निकालना पड़े। पैसे दोनों जगह हैं; दूसरे रास्ते में 1 extra step है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration only: bank account → ₹300 payment; selected PO access → cash withdrawal → ₹300 payment. Not a universal current restriction.

beats.say: यह hypothetical है, universal restriction नहीं। रकम निकाल सकना liquidity है; payment के steps convenience बदलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical access paths; availability versus access steps.

beats.say: Fairly liquid और slightly less convenient साथ हो सकते हैं। Less convenient का मतलब inaccessible नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Less convenient ≠ inaccessible.

beats.say: Post Office savings fairly liquid हैं, ordinary bank deposits से थोड़ी कम convenient; availability और access अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: Comparison table: liquidity and relative convenience.

beats.say: Account से ₹1000 agreed date तक अलग रखो तो payment-ready रकम क्या होगी? जल्दी निकालने पर शर्तें हो सकती हैं। ऐसी bank रकम Time Deposits है; FD और recurring deposits इसके examples हैं।
beats.on_screen: Demand account transfers ₹1000 into an agreed-term holding. Conditional premature access; reveal Time Deposits, FD and recurring deposits after the situation.

beats.say: Broadest coverage, reporting importance नहीं है। Broadest label अकेला component formula नहीं देता।
beats.on_screen: Breadth label versus component formula and reporting role.

beats.say: M1 ₹5000 में bank time deposits ₹6000 जोड़ो: ₹11000, यानी M3 या Broad Money। फिर Post Office savings ₹2000 और दूसरे eligible deposits ₹3000 जोड़ो: ₹16000, यानी M4; NSC बाहर है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical contributions, OD zero. Calculate before revealing M3 and M4 labels; NSC card excluded. PO savings counted once.

beats.say: M3 important money-supply measure है; news में growth आम तौर पर इसी की होती है। M4 broadest है। Recurring deposits यानी नियमित किस्तों की बचत भी bank time deposits में आती है।
beats.on_screen: Mock M3 growth headline; M3 importance versus M4 breadth; FD, RD and other bank time deposits.

beats.say: ₹1000 demand से FD में करो: demand ₹3000, time ₹7000। M1 ₹4000 हुआ; M3 ₹11000 रहा, क्योंकि दोनों components उसमें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Reset original hypothetical holdings. Demand ₹4000 → ₹3000; time ₹6000 → ₹7000; M3 unchanged.

beats.say: अलग snapshots में M3 ₹1000 crore स्थिर, eligible Post Office deposits ₹200 से ₹250 crore हों: M4 ₹1200 से ₹1250 crore होगा।
beats.on_screen: Same-date stocks per snapshot; common crore-rupee unit; NSC excluded.

beats.say: यह assumed accounting comparison है, transfer से money creation नहीं। Broadest coverage, important reporting और जमीन समेत total wealth अलग बातें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Breadth ≠ importance ≠ total wealth.

beats.say: M3 = M1 + bank time deposits, M2 नहीं। M4 = M3 + all qualifying Post Office deposits, excluding NSC; savings दोबारा मत जोड़ना।
beats.on_screen: Build formulas term by term; count eligible savings once.

beats.say: नया loan क्या बदलता है? ₹100 loan deposit बना, supplier ने bank में रखा; बाकी बदलाव न हों तो M3 ₹1000 से ₹1100 हुआ।
beats.on_screen: New lending increases illustrative M3 by ₹100.

beats.say: Certificate से किराना दोगे? ₹2000 cash में से ₹1000 का NSC खरीदो: cash ₹1000 बचेगा; खरीदारी में वही इस्तेमाल होगा, certificate नहीं।
पहला example RBI की M3 monitoring समझाता है। दूसरा NSC exclusion: वह long-term savings instrument है, readily spendable money नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Two reasoning tracks: monitoring and exclusion.

beats.say: M3 से liquidity और credit growth के संकेत मिलते हैं। यानी account balances और lending साथ जाँचेंगे; खरीदने की ताकत सामान से तेज़ बढ़े तो दामों पर दबाव बन सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Compare account balances and lending; then compare spending power with available goods, using a conditional price-pressure arrow.

beats.say: Policy effectiveness का check है: RBI के कदमों के बाद money, credit और prices चाही दिशा में गए? NSC लंबे समय की saving है, आज का payment balance नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Policy dashboard checks intended direction; separate long-term certificate from today's payment balance.

beats.say: M3 के साथ credit और prices जाँचो। Post Office label काफी नहीं; NSC बाहर है।
beats.on_screen: M3 alongside credit and price data; NSC excluded.

beats.say: M3 बढ़ना inflation का proof नहीं; यह loans का total भी नहीं। NSC बाहर होने से सारे long-term deposits बाहर नहीं होते।
beats.on_screen: Reject deterministic inflation and blanket long-term-deposit exclusion.

beats.say: RBI के checks हैं inflationary pressures, liquidity, credit growth और policy effectiveness। NSC long-term, readily spendable नहीं; इसलिए M4 से बाहर है।
beats.on_screen: Four monitoring gauges; NSC exclusion chain.

beats.say: जाँचो: किसका balance, कहाँ, कौन-सा product? M0 अलग है; M2 और M3 का base M1 है। Form बदलना money creation नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Final holder–institution–product checklist and aggregate map.

notes.about: This unit teaches the coverage, formulas and uses of M0–M4, separating reserve money from public monetary holdings. Its strongest teaching device is distinguishing a change in composition from money creation.
key_questions: Which balances enter each aggregate, and which are excluded?
Why do transfers sometimes leave an aggregate unchanged?
Why is M3 important while M4 is broadest?
